key_insight: The paper presents a unified neural inference pipeline that jointly chooses the most plausible chemical reaction network and estimates its kinetic parameters from time-series experiments.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more scalable simulation-based inference for reaction engineering problems where multiple mechanisms fit the same data.
method: Shared 1D-CNNs learn compact features from variable-length time-series experiments.
A permutation-invariant Set Attention module aggregates multi-experiment information into low-dimensional summaries.
These summaries feed a model-selection network plus model-specific conditional INNs for posterior parameter estimation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on a real protodeboronation case, showing the method can resolve competing catalyst deactivation pathways and recover kinetic parameters.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and diversity of simulated training data, and the added model-selection step can be sensitive when candidate mechanisms are highly similar.
paper_title: Joint Neural Posterior Estimation and Model Selection for Chemical Reaction Networks
